title: One base unit donated to the module permanently blocks every buy (absolute-balance I1 check)
description: SleeveBuy.execute calls _requireNothingHeld(usdg) and _requireNothingHeld(token) (lines 39-40), which revert ModuleHoldsFunds when asset.balanceOf(address(this)) != 0 (lines 115-118). That checks the module's absolute balance, not the change this call made. Anyone can send USDG or a stock token straight to the module address with a plain transfer, outside any module call. The module is immutable, has no sweep, and can't refuse an incoming ERC-20 transfer.
scenario: Attacker calls USDG.transfer(sleeveModule, 1). From then on every executeBuy reverts ModuleHoldsFunds(USDG, 1), so every split whose guard says BUY reverts for every account, and every settle reverts too. Sending 1 wei of SPY does the same for every SPY buy. Confirmed by test/audit/reentrancy_DustAndForgedRevert.t.sol: test_dustDonationBricksEveryBuy and test_tokenDustDonationBricksTickerBuys both pass. A sell-back that copies this check would be blocked the same way.
impact: The core product stops working for every user, permanently, for 0.000001 USDG. Recovery means deploying a new module and having every account reinstall. Funds are not lost: USDG stays spendable and buckets can still be released. That is why this is HIGH and not CRITICAL, but it is unrecoverable on this deploy. By the rubric's DoS wording it could be argued down to MEDIUM.
fix: Measure I1 as a delta. Read the module's USDG and token balances before executeFromExecutor in _swap and revert only if either balance went up after the batch (after > before). Apply the same pattern to the future sell. Update the I1 wording and tests to say the module gains nothing in any call.

title: A 1-base-unit donation to the module permanently blocks every buy on the immutable module
description: SleeveBuy.execute checks `asset.balanceOf(address(this)) != 0` for USDG and the stock token after every swap (lines 39-40, 115-118) and reverts ModuleHoldsFunds. That's an absolute check, not a delta. Anyone can transfer USDG or a stock token to the module address. The module is immutable and has no sweep, so the balance can never go back to zero. _buy only catches PremiumAboveCap, so the revert bubbles out and the whole split or settle fails.
scenario: An attacker, or a user who mistakes the module for their Sleeve address, sends 1 base unit of USDG (1e-6 USD) or 1 wei of SPY to the module. From then on every split whose guard passes reverts ModuleHoldsFunds(usdg, 1), and every settle does the same. Verified by contracts/test/audit/funds_Donation.t.sol (both tests pass). Splits only succeed when the guard queues, so all equity ends up in buckets that can never settle. Component 6's sell-back will hit the same wall if it reuses this check.
impact: Every account loses the product for good: no Stock Token buys and no sorting during market hours. The only fix is to redeploy the module, then reinstall on every account and migrate. USDG stays in the accounts and owners can release or uninstall, so nothing is stolen, but the core function is gone for about a microdollar.
fix: Read the module's USDG and token balances before executeFromExecutor and require them unchanged afterward (after == before). That enforces I1 for the module's own actions without making the absolute balance a kill switch. Record the donation case in DECISIONS.md, since the PRD wording of I1 ('holds no USDG before or after any call') can't be enforced against third-party transfers.

title: One wei of USDG or of a stock token sent to the module permanently bricks every buy
description: SleeveBuy.execute calls _requireNothingHeld(usdg) and _requireNothingHeld(order.token) (lines 39-40), which revert ModuleHoldsFunds when the module's balance of the asset is non-zero. The check is absolute rather than a before/after delta, and the module has no sweep. USDG has no transfer restriction on contract recipients, and Stock.transfer only checks the blocklist, so anyone can push dust to the module address. SleeveTrade._buy (line 438) rethrows every revert except PremiumAboveCap, so ModuleHoldsFunds reverts the whole split or settle.
scenario: An attacker transfers 1 base unit of USDG to SleeveModule. From then on, every split whose guard reaches the buy step, for every account, reverts ModuleHoldsFunds, and every settle does too. Sending 1 wei of SPY to the module does the same for every SPY buy. The PoC at contracts/test/audit/funds_Donation.t.sol (test_oneWeiUsdgDonationBricksEverySplitBuy, test_oneWeiTokenDonationBricksSettle) passes against the snapshot. I re-ran it with FOUNDRY_OUT=out-tokens.
impact: The core product stops working for good, globally, for 1 wei of cost. The module is immutable (D-019), so the only way out is a new module and every account reinstalling. No funds are lost: release and owner outflows still work, and splits that queue still run. While the guard is clear, payments stay unsorted and public triggers revert, so the grief is also cheap to keep going.
fix: Snapshot usdg.balanceOf(address(this)) and token.balanceOf(address(this)) before the executeFromExecutor batch and require that neither went up. That enforces 'the call left nothing in the module' instead of 'the module holds nothing'. Do the same in the component 6 sell path. Restate I1 in the PRD/SPEC as a per-call delta, since the absolute form cannot hold against donations.

title: One wei of USDG or a stock token sent to the module permanently bricks every buy for every account
description: SleeveBuy.execute calls _requireNothingHeld(usdg) and _requireNothingHeld(token) (lines 39-40), which revert ModuleHoldsFunds whenever balanceOf(module) != 0. It checks an absolute balance, not the change across the batch. SleeveModule has no sweep function and can't be upgraded (D-019), so a balance anyone sends to it stays forever. SleeveTrade._buy only catches PremiumAboveCap, so ModuleHoldsFunds bubbles up and the whole split or settle reverts. Nothing queues and the spend share isn't credited either.
scenario: Right after the mainnet deploy, an attacker transfers 1 base unit of USDG to the SleeveModule address. Every later split whose guard clears to BUY reverts ModuleHoldsFunds(usdg, 1), and so does every settle. Sending 1 wei of SPY (bought from the pool or transferred from any holder) does the same for every SPY buy. Existing PoCs: test/audit/funds_Donation.t.sol and test/audit/reentrancy_DustAndForgedRevert.t.sol::test_dustDonationBricksEveryBuy, both passing on this snapshot.
impact: Permanent, unrecoverable DoS of the core product (payday split and settle) for every installed account. It costs the attacker under a cent. Funds aren't locked, because unsorted USDG stays spendable in brackets and buckets can be released, but the module has to be redeployed and every user has to reinstall. I1 is also unreachable after the donation, since the module 'holds funds' it can never remove.
fix: Measure I1 as a delta. Read usdg.balanceOf(module) and token.balanceOf(module) before the executeFromExecutor batch and require both to be unchanged afterwards (revert ModuleHoldsFunds(asset, after - before) on any increase). Keep the stronger absolute check only in tests. Use the same delta form for the sell path in component 6.

title: One base unit donated to the module permanently bricks every buy for every account (absolute I1 check)
description: _requireNothingHeld reverts ModuleHoldsFunds when usdg.balanceOf(module) != 0 or token.balanceOf(module) != 0. It checks an absolute balance, not the delta of this call. The module has no sweep, isn't upgradeable, and anyone can transfer USDG or a stock token to it. The revert isn't PremiumAboveCap, so SleeveTrade._buy bubbles it and the whole split or settle reverts.
scenario: An attacker sends 1 base unit of USDG to the SleeveModule address. From then on, every split whose equity part reaches the buy branch, and every settle that would buy, reverts with ModuleHoldsFunds(usdg, 1), for every installed account. Sending 1 wei of a stock token to the module bricks that ticker the same way. The existing PoC test/audit/funds_Donation.t.sol passes against the snapshot. I re-ran it.
impact: The core product (investing part of each payment) stops for good, at a cost of 1 base unit. No funds are lost. Unsorted USDG stays unsorted, buckets can still be released by the owner, and refusal paths still work. Recovery needs a new module deploy plus every user uninstalling and reinstalling. Component 6 sell-back will inherit this if it reuses the helper. I1 is literally violated by anyone, without any module call.
fix: Measure I1 as a delta: read usdg.balanceOf(address(this)) and token.balanceOf(address(this)) before the executeFromExecutor batch and require each after-balance to be <= its before-balance. That proves the call left nothing behind. Optionally add a permissionless sweep that sends stray module balances to a fixed sink, so the absolute I1 can be restored. Apply the same delta rule in the sell-back path.

title: Unscheduled closure or market-wide halt: the held price passes as live for the whole day
description: readStockFeed rejects a round only when it is older than 25 hours or older than sessionOpenedAt. The calendar only knows about a closure if the timelock added it before 00:00Z on the day (SessionCalendarExtension.addClosure, line 188). The extension's own comment says a closure announced later "is guarded only by PriceGuard" (line 181), but PriceGuard does not catch it. A full-day closure lasts at most 24 hours, which is under the 25-hour max age, and the last round still postdates the Sunday open. So for the whole closed day the guard returns NONE on a frozen price. Trading halts behave the same way, including a level-3 circuit breaker that ends the day and a single-stock news halt. oraclePaused could flag these, but chain-constants shows it has never been used.
scenario: An event like Hurricane Sandy or a short-notice national day of mourning closes NYSE and the 24 Hour Market on a Wednesday, and the timelock misses the addClosure deadline. The NVDA feed stops at Tue 19:59 EDT. The calendar still says Wednesday is open. A payment lands, and the keeper splits, or a public caller after the grace, on a pool trading on news while the feed is frozen. The fill passes at up to premiumCap above the held price, and Thursday reopens 10% lower. PoC: test/audit/oracle_HeldPrice.t.sol shows a round 24h old, from before an unlisted closure, accepted with Reason.NONE.
impact: The equity share is bought against a held price that the PRD's weekend and holiday guard was meant to exclude. The owner takes the reopen gap, which is the exact risk 'Weekend or holiday gap: equity share queues' was written to remove. Each unscheduled closure or halt exposes up to about 25 hours of payments.
fix: Add a liveness test that does not depend on the calendar. One option: during a session, require the newest updatedAt across all active tickers' feeds to be within a market-liveness bound, for example 13 to 16 hours. In the week of rounds pulled for this audit (notes/oracle_week_rounds.txt), the longest gap across all four feeds in session was about 12h, Thu 15:50 to Fri 04:01 EDT. Another option: a same-day closure path that skips the long timelock delay but can only close, never open. At a minimum, fix the comment at SessionCalendarExtension.sol:181 and record the gap in SECURITY.md and DECISIONS.md.

title: Lots are never reconciled with the account's stock-token balance, so sell-back will act on phantom lots
description: createLot records tokensBought and tokensRemaining from the measured fill. After that, nothing ties a lot to the account's actual token balance. Owner brackets (SleeveModule._bookOwnerOp, line 412) only measure USDG, so a bracketed owner batch that transfers or sells stock tokens leaves every lot FILLED with full tokensRemaining. PRD section 9 explicitly lets the owner transfer stock tokens through any ERC-4337 client. SPEC 12 has sell(lotId or amount) decrement lots and say tokens outside lots are not sellable (D-009 Q30), but the module can't tell lot tokens from other tokens by balance. Component 6 has no lot-versus-balance invariant to rely on.
scenario: The owner gets lot 7 with 10 SPY, then moves the 10 SPY out in a bracketed batch. Lot 7 still shows 10 tokensRemaining, and the app, verifier and receipts show holdings that don't exist. Later 4 SPY arrive from outside Sleeve. sell(SPY, 4, 0, ...) sells those 4 non-lot tokens, contradicting Q30, and writes PART_SOLD receipts against lot 7 that attribute proceeds to tokens that left long ago. If the balance is short, the swap reverts with an opaque error.
impact: Wrong accounting on the trust surface (receipts and lots) that never corrects itself, and a spec deviation from D-009 Q30 and the PRD conservation check. No direct loss, because only the owner can sell.
fix: In component 6, cap each sell at min(sum of lots' tokensRemaining, token.balanceOf(account)), and measure tokensIn by balance delta as the buy does. Add an owner-callable or automatic lot reconcile that trims tokensRemaining oldest-first or newest-first to the balance, with a receipt. Alternatively, extend the bracket to snapshot the balances of the tokens with lots and book a negative delta against them. Document that lots are an upper bound until reconciled.

title: The lot transition rule forbids PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD, so a lot can only be partly sold once
description: transitionLot allows FILLED/SETTLED to PART_SOLD/SOLD and PART_SOLD to SOLD only. SPEC section 12 says each lot a sell touches gets a PART_SOLD or SOLD receipt, and sell-by-amount walks lots oldest first. A second partial sale of a lot that is already PART_SOLD needs PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD, which reverts BadLotTransition.
scenario: An owner sells 3 of a 10-token lot (FILLED to PART_SOLD), then tries to sell 2 more. Sell-by-amount starts at the head lot, still PART_SOLD with 7 left, and the transition reverts. Verified by contracts/test/audit/funds_LotTransition.t.sol. After the first partial sale the owner can only sell that lot's whole remainder, or sell a specific later lot by id.
impact: Sell-back, the owner's main way back to USDG through Sleeve, fails for any partial amount smaller than the head lot's remainder. Since tokens outside lots aren't sellable through Sleeve in M0 (D-009 Q30), owners have to over-sell or leave Sleeve to reach their tokens.
fix: Allow PART_SOLD to PART_SOLD in transitionLot, or have component 6 skip the status write when the status doesn't change. Either way, update SPEC section 14 and I7's allowed-transition list so the tests encode it.

title: Dust transfers keep the public trigger from ever firing for split and settle
description: observe() restarts observedAt whenever unsorted grows past observedUnsorted (lines 73-77). A public split needs unsorted <= observedUnsorted and the grace since observedAt (_requireSplitGrace, 509-514), and a public settle takes the latest of since, openedAt and observedAt (518-526). So any growth in unsorted, even 1 base unit, voids or restarts the clock for USDG that has already waited past the grace. Any keeper split also clears the observation (530-534), which restarts the public settle clock for buckets that have nothing to do with that split. PRD 7.2 and the PRD 9 failure table promise that anyone can trigger once unsorted USDG has waited past the grace, and that this is the fallback when the keeper is down. Q15 guards against pre-aging the clock but not against pushing it back.
scenario: PoC: contracts/test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol, tests test_dustEvery50MinutesBlocksPublicSplitIndefinitely and test_dustPlusObserveBlocksPublicSettleIndefinitely, both pass. A payment is observed at t0. A griefer sends 1 base unit of USDG every 50 minutes and calls observe(). Nine hours later the public split still reverts GracePeriodActive(now + 3600). A queued bucket observed the same way stays refused to a public settle.
impact: The public liveness fallback can be blocked for good for about 1e-6 USDG plus gas per hour. The owner trigger still works, so funds aren't locked, but when the keeper is down the spec'd anyone-can-trigger path is gone. A compromised keeper can do the same to public settles by sending dust and running keeper splits.
fix: Don't let growth void an elapsed clock. Either let a PUBLIC split sort only min(unsorted, observedUnsorted) once observedAt + grace has passed, leaving the excess unsorted on its own clock, or keep two observation slots (matured and pending). Give public settle a clock that observe() and keeper splits don't reset while pending > 0, for example one set only when it is zero. Add a test for this grief next to test_split_dustTransferCannotPreAgeTheObservation.

title: Dust plus observe() lets any stranger postpone the public split and settle fallback indefinitely
description: observe() restarts observedAt whenever unsorted exceeds observedUnsorted. A public split needs unsorted <= observedUnsorted and observedAt + grace (_requireSplitGrace, line 509). A public settle's readyAt includes observedAt (_settleReadyAt, line 523). Also, every sort or settle clears the observation for the whole account (_clearObservation, line 530), so one bucket's settle or a dust split resets the clock for every other bucket and for unsorted USDG. The public trigger is the only liveness path when the keeper is down, and a stranger can keep moving it forward for the price of 1 base unit of USDG and an observe() call each hour.
scenario: The keeper is offline. A 500 USDG payment is observed at t0. Every 50 minutes the attacker sends 1 base unit of USDG to the account and calls observe(), which bumps observedAt. At t0 + 10h a public split still reverts GracePeriodActive. The same works for a queued bucket: dust plus observe() pushes the settle readyAt forward, because observedAt is part of max(since, openedAt, observedAt). PoC: test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol (both tests pass on this snapshot).
impact: The anyone-can-trigger fallback that PRD and SPEC rely on when the keeper fails can be held off for as long as the attacker keeps paying a few cents an hour. Owner funds stay spendable and releasable, but splits and buys don't happen without an owner action.
fix: Drop observedAt from public settle readiness entirely: max(bucket.since, sessionOpenedAt) + grace already anchors it, and dust can't move bucket.since. For split, either let a public split sort only min(unsorted, observedUnsorted) once the grace has passed, leaving later arrivals for their own clock, or keep the original observedAt and record growth as a second (amount, time) pair, so growth doesn't reset the clock for the amount already covered. Then _clearObservation should clear only what the action consumed.

title: Caller-chosen quote makes the slippage cap meaningless for keeper and public triggers, so every buy can be pushed to the premium cap
description: minOut = amount * quote / 1e6 * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000, where quote is whatever the trigger passes. _enter only checks quote != 0. With quote = 1, minOut is close to 0. For KEEPER and PUBLIC triggers, the only bound on price is exceedsPremium against the Chainlink answer. That answer can trail the live price by up to 0.5% (deviation threshold), and USDG can sit 0.5% from peg (see the next finding). The rule's slippageBps, which defaults to 50 bps and is shown to the owner as a guard, does nothing unless the owner triggers. On FCFS ordering an outside sandwich isn't possible, but a self-sandwich is: one contract call can push the pool, call split or settle with quote=1, and unwind.
scenario: After the grace, an attacker contract buys the token in an allowlisted thin pool until the price sits just under answer*(1+cap). It then calls split(account, pool, 1), the account buys at that price, and the attacker sells back into the higher price. A stolen keeper key can do the same on every split right away with no grace, even though PRD 14 says it has 'no authority beyond public functions'.
impact: The PRD's 'worst case' of about 1.5% at the default cap becomes the expected case for any non-owner trigger, and up to about 5.5 to 6% at the 500 bps maximum cap. Value goes to the trigger, minus pool fees. Loss is bounded by the cap, which PRD 7.4 accepts as the residual bound, but the slippage setting owners see doesn't protect them.
fix: Tie minOut to the feed on-chain for non-owner triggers: minOut = max(quoted minOut, amount * 10^20 / answer * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000), or reject a quote below the feed-implied quote by more than slippageBps. That turns the 50 bps slippage cap into the real bound. Otherwise, document in the app and SECURITY.md that slippage only applies to owner triggers.

title: Anyone can hold off the public trigger indefinitely by donating dust and calling observe
description: observe(account) is permissionless and restarts the public-trigger clock (observedAt = now) whenever unsorted exceeds observedUnsorted. A griefer can send 1 base unit of USDG to the account so unsorted grows by 1, then call observe. That restarts the clock. _requireSplitGrace (line 509) and _settleReadyAt (line 518) both run from observedAt, so the public split and the public settle never reach the grace. D-009 Q15 only stops dust from pre-aging the clock. Using dust to keep pushing it back is not addressed.
scenario: The keeper is down, or the owner set keeper to zero. An account has 500 USDG unsorted and someone calls observe. Every 59 minutes the griefer transfers 1 base unit (0.000001 USDG) to the account and calls observe. Each public split reverts GracePeriodActive. PoC test/audit/access_Observe.t.sol::test_access_dustObserveBlocksPublicSplitForever keeps the public split blocked for 24 rounds at a cost of 24 base units plus gas.
impact: This breaks the PRD 7.x and section 9 liveness fallback ('Keeper down: anyone can trigger after the grace period') for sorting and for settling buckets. Funds stay spendable and the owner can still trigger, so nothing is lost, but the equity share can be kept from buying for as long as the griefer keeps paying cents of gas.
fix: Don't move an existing clock forward. Keep observedAt and observedUnsorted once set, and let a PUBLIC split sort at most observedUnsorted, leaving any later growth unsorted for its own observation in a second slot. Alternatively, restart only when the growth is at least MIN_CLIP_FLOOR. For settle, base readyAt on the bucket's since and the session opening and not on an observation that dust can move.

title: onUninstall release costs about 250k+ gas, and a short callGasLimit silently skips it while Kernel still removes the module
description: onUninstall releases every non-empty bucket, writing a RELEASED receipt for each (hash SSTORE, a full-receipt event, TokenSource and calendar reads). Measured on the unit harness with four launch buckets and warm slots: 250,271 gas, so cold on chain it's higher. Kernel v3.1 calls onUninstall through ExcessivelySafeCall with gasleft() and ignores the result (g6-notes section 7). If the UserOp's callGasLimit leaves Kernel its last 1/64 but not enough for the release, the module is removed with ModuleUninstallResult(false), and SleeveModule keeps installed=true, pendingTotal and the buckets, with no RELEASED receipts and no Uninstalled event.
scenario: An owner uninstalls through a sponsored UserOp with a tight callGasLimit while four buckets are pending. PoC test/audit/dos_UninstallAndLots.t.sol::test_shortGasUninstallLeavesStaleState: MockAccount.uninstallModule{gas:120_000} completes, module.isInitialized stays true and pendingTotal stays 120e6.
impact: No funds are lost, since USDG stays in the account and onInstall cleans the stale state on reinstall. The app, verifier and receipts show buckets that were never released, and the uninstall emits no Uninstalled event. Bounded by the ticker count, which is 4 at launch.
fix: Have the app set the uninstall callGasLimit from previewed bucket count times about 90k plus margin, and check ModuleUninstallResult. Better, have the app release buckets in the same bracketed batch before uninstallModule, so onUninstall is cheap. Document the gas band in GAS.md next to the measured release.

title: The planned sell-back guard misses the router blocklist, which Stock.approve and transferFrom enforce
description: checkToken tests isBlocked(account) and isBlocked(pool) only. On a buy that's enough, because the pool calls transfer(account). On a sell-back, Stock.approve checks the spender (SwapRouter02), and the pool callback's transferFrom checks msg.sender (the router), the account and the pool (chain-constants section 3). SPEC section 12's mirrored sell guard lists only 'account not blocked', so if component 6 reuses checkToken unchanged, a blocked router turns every sell into an opaque Blocked(address) revert. It never becomes a named SellWaits or refusal.
scenario: The issuer's BLOCKER_ROLE adds SwapRouter02 to the shared registry blocklist. Every sell-back for every ticker reverts inside the account batch with the token's Blocked(router), and the app can't explain why.
impact: The only M0 cash-out path through Sleeve fails with an unnamed error. The owner can still move tokens directly, so no funds are locked.
fix: For the sell path, add isBlocked(router) next to the account and pool checks and revert a named error, for example RouterBlocked. Add a fork test with the registry blocking the router.

title: No post-change multiplier check: the immediate updateMultiplier form never queues, and a pre-change feed round is accepted right after effectiveAt
description: checkMultiplier returns NONE whenever effectiveAt <= block.timestamp. The issuer's updateMultiplier(uint256) sets effectiveAt = block.timestamp (chain-constants section 3), so an immediate change never hits PRD 7.4 step 5, even though it 'takes effect inside the guard window'. For scheduled changes, the guard queues only until effectiveAt and then accepts a round whose updatedAt is before effectiveAt. Dividend steps are under 0.5%, so the feed isn't forced to post a new round. Research Q1 raised this and D-014 chose no after-clause. In theory per-token value is continuous through a split, so the risk only shows up if the feed's round and the switched multiplier disagree. If they do, nothing bounds the error, and oraclePaused, the other corporate-action guard, has never been used.
scenario: The issuer applies a 1:2 reverse split with the immediate form. If the feed's next round lags or is computed from mismatched parts, the guard clears, because effectiveAt == now gives NONE and the round is fresh by age. A fill priced against a wrong answer then passes the cap. PoC: test/audit/oracle_Multiplier.t.sol, where both the immediate change and effectiveAt+0 pass with a round from before the change.
impact: The PRD threat row 'Corporate action in progress: pending-multiplier checks, queue' doesn't hold for immediate changes or for the minutes after a scheduled one. Exposure depends on how the feed is built.
fix: In checkBuy, after readStockFeed, return MULTIPLIER (or STALE) when effectiveAt != 0 && effectiveAt <= block.timestamp && updatedAt < effectiveAt. This queues until the first round after the switch, at most one heartbeat. It also covers the immediate form. Change the step-5 test to effectiveAt >= block.timestamp so the same-block case is caught too.

title: Reopen freshness test uses updatedAt (transmit time), not startedAt (observation time)
description: The B2-2 rule rejects a round with updatedAt < sessionOpenedAt. On these OCR2 DualAggregators, startedAt is the observation timestamp and updatedAt is the transmit time, which ran 12 seconds later on every sampled round (chain-constants section 4). A round observed before the reopen but transmitted after it passes as a round from the new session, even though it carries the held price.
scenario: At Sunday 20:00:00 EDT, a round observed at 19:59:55 and transmitted at 20:00:07 shows the Friday price with updatedAt >= sessionOpenedAt. The keeper's settle at the open, which PRD 7.4 says runs 'at session open and when fresh rounds arrive', buys against it. Observed reopen rounds landed 23 to 48s after 20:00, so the window is narrow.
impact: A held weekend price can, in a narrow window, be treated as the first live round. Exposure is limited to the reopen gap times the cap logic, and it's unlikely if the DON doesn't observe while the market is closed.
fix: Use startedAt for the reopen comparison: require startedAt >= sessionOpenedAt, plus the existing updatedAt checks. It costs nothing, since latestRoundData already returns it. Record startedAt in the receipt or derive it in the verifier.

title: Premium cap compares USDG spent with a USD feed price, ignoring the USDG/USD answer it already read
description: exceedsPremium and premiumBps treat 1 USDG as 1 USD. checkUsdg accepts USDG anywhere in [0.995, 1.005], and the guard keeps usdgAnswer but never uses it in the arithmetic. With USDG above peg, each USDG spent is worth more USD, so the effective cap against the USD reference is roughly cap + (usdgAnswer - 1). Receipts also report premiumBps on that basis.
scenario: USDG/USD is at 1.0049, inside the band, and the feed trails the live price by 0.5%. A fill at exactly the 100 bps cap costs about 2.0% over the live USD price, not the 'about 1.5 percent' worst case PRD 7.4 states and the app shows (S34). At the 500 bps maximum it's about 6%.
impact: The stated worst case is understated by up to 50 bps, and the receipt's premium is not the USD premium. The loss is bounded and small.
fix: Convert the reference into USDG before comparing: answerUsdg = answer * 10^8 / usdgAnswer, using 512-bit math as elsewhere. Or add the usdgAnswer factor to both sides of exceedsPremium and premiumBps, and put usdgAnswer into BuyOrder. Otherwise, restate the worst case as cap + 0.5% feed lag + 0.5% depeg band in the PRD, the app and SECURITY.md.

title: The minimum-out check (PRD step 9) runs before the premium check (step 8), so a fill above the cap reverts where the spec says it queues
description: PRD 7.4 orders step 8 (premium cap: queue the equity) before step 9 (trigger's minimum: revert). The router gets amountOutMinimum = minOut (line 105), and _swap checks TooFewTokens (line 75) before the premium is measured (lines 42-53). When both fail, the call reverts 'Too little received' instead of queueing PREMIUM.
scenario: PoC test_minOutIsCheckedBeforeThePremium in contracts/test/audit/spec_PublicGraceGrief.t.sol passes. With the pool priced 150 bps above the feed, the keeper's quote queues PREMIUM, but the same split with quote*2 reverts with 'Too little received'.
impact: Safe, since nothing moves, but the guard order differs from PRD 7.4 and SPEC 9 step 9. A pool pushed between the quote and inclusion reverts instead of queueing, so the keeper has to retry rather than getting a PREMIUM receipt.
fix: Pass amountOutMinimum 0 to the router (the sqrtPriceLimit stays 0) and check minOut in SleeveBuy after exceedsPremium, reverting TooFewTokens there. Or record the reordering in DECISIONS and SPEC 9.

title: Lots aren't tied to token balances and survive uninstall, so sell-back plumbing can point at tokens that are gone
description: createLot records tokensBought and tokensRemaining from the measured fill. Nothing lowers tokensRemaining when the owner moves Stock Tokens out outside Sleeve, and onUninstall keeps lots and lotQueues (SPEC section 6). On reinstall the old lots are back at the queue head even if the tokens left while the module was uninstalled.
scenario: An owner holds a 10-token SPY lot, uninstalls, transfers 10 SPY to an exchange, reinstalls, and buys a new 5-token lot. A sell-by-amount of 5 tokens walks oldest first, picks the empty lot 1, and the swap's transferFrom reverts. Only selling by the new lot's id works.
impact: Component 6 sells can revert or report PART_SOLD/SOLD receipts against tokens that left outside Sleeve.
fix: In component 6, cap each lot's sellable amount at min(tokensRemaining, the account's token balance not claimed by later lots), or skip lots whose tokens are gone. Or mark lots stale at uninstall. Add a fork test where tokens leave outside Sleeve before a sell.

title: Lot queues grow without bound per account and ticker, and a by-amount sell writes one receipt per lot in a single call
description: createLot pushes every FILLED or SETTLED buy onto lotQueues[account][tickerId].ids, and nothing ever pops it, since SOLD lots stay behind head. SPEC 12 has a by-amount sell walk lots oldest-first and write a PART_SOLD or SOLD receipt per touched lot, and it reverts ExceedsLots unless one call covers the amount. A receipt write alone measured 45,225 gas warm (dos_UninstallAndLots.t.sol::test_receiptWriteGas), so with lot updates and the swap, a sell touching a few hundred lots reaches bundler callGasLimits and then the 32M Arbitrum per-tx limit. lotsOf() also returns the whole ids array, which keeps growing for the app and verifier.
scenario: A merchant-style account receiving many small payments (for example the campaign rule at 50 percent and a 1 USDG clip, with the keeper splitting each payment) builds up thousands of SPY lots. A 'sell everything' by amount runs out of gas. An attacker can add lots too, but each one costs at least minClip/equityBps USDG gifted to the victim, so the risk is mostly organic.
impact: Component 6's by-amount sell can fail for heavy accounts. The owner can still sell lot by lot, so nothing is locked, but the main sell path degrades. lotsOf eth_calls get heavy.
fix: In component 6, give sell a maxLots bound (or let by-amount sells partially fill up to N lots and return the remainder), keep advancing head over SOLD lots, and emit per-lot fills in one aggregate receipt or event rather than one full receipt each. Add a paged lotsOf(account, ticker, start, count) view that starts at head.

title: A zero equity part writes QUEUED with reason CLIP while nothing is queued
description: setRule accepts equityBps 0 (validateShares(10000, 0) passes), and dust payments under a non-zero rule can give equityPart 0. _sort then writes status QUEUED, reason CLIP and usdgQueued 0, and leaves the bucket alone. PRD 7.6 and SPEC 9 step 7 define QUEUED as equity entering pending. This receipt says the money waits when all of it went to spend.
scenario: The owner sets a 100 percent spend rule (10000/0). Every payment produces a QUEUED(CLIP) receipt. PoC test_zeroEquityRuleWritesQueuedClipWithNothingQueued confirms it, and the repo's own test_split_zeroEquityPart_sortsEverythingToSpendWithoutTheGuard encodes it.
impact: The inbox, history, five-day queue prompt and verifier will show money waiting that isn't. A misleading trust surface.
fix: Reject equityBps == 0 in _validateRule (an ACTIVE rule implies an equity share), and for dust give a zero equity part a distinct outcome, such as reason NONE with usdgQueued 0. Document whichever you pick in SPEC 13.

title: An equity part below the clip strands in its bucket once a later payment fills directly
description: A split whose equity part is under minClip queues it in the ticker's bucket with reason CLIP. A later split whose equity part clears the clip buys only its own part (the _buy path) and leaves the bucket alone. settle reverts BelowClip for any bucket under minClip (line 273). The bucket only grows if another sub-clip part happens to arrive.
scenario: Default rule: 10 percent to SPY, 25 USDG clip. A 100 USDG payment queues 10 USDG with CLIP. A 1,000 USDG payment then fills 100 USDG directly. The 10 USDG bucket can't be settled by the keeper or the public. Verified by contracts/test/audit/funds_Liveness.t.sol::test_subClipBucketStrandsAfterALaterFill.
impact: The owner's equity share is never invested, and it counts as pending, not spend, until the owner notices and releases it. Nothing is lost.
fix: In _sort, when the guard clears and the rule ticker's bucket is non-empty, add the bucket to the buy amount (settle it along with the split). Or let settle run when bucket plus nothing else is below the clip but the current split's equity part would cover it.

title: RECONCILED receipts repurpose usdgSpent and usdgQueued
description: _reconcile sets usdgIn = fromSpend + fromPending, usdgSpent = fromSpend (USDG taken off the spend ledger) and usdgQueued = fromPending (USDG taken off buckets). Everywhere else, usdgSpent means equity USDG paid to the venue and usdgQueued means USDG added to pending. SPEC 13 and D-019 only say 'totals'. A consumer that sums usdgSpent as invested capital, or checks I2 per receipt, will read a third-party pull as a buy.
scenario: An old approval pulls 50 USDG. The next split writes RECONCILED with usdgSpent 50 and usdgQueued 0. The app's 'equity bought' total and the verifier's per-status math pick up 50 USDG of phantom investment.
impact: Wrong numbers in the UI and verifier unless every consumer special-cases RECONCILED. PRD 7.10 and the README numbers rule depend on these being right.
fix: Document the RECONCILED field mapping in SPEC 13, or add explicit fields (or reuse usdgOut and tokensIn semantics) so usdgSpent keeps one meaning. Add a verifier vector for RECONCILED.

title: A trigger's pool off a non-empty allowlist reverts PoolNotAllowed, where SPEC 9 and PRD 7.4 say REFUSED_TICKER, and no DECISIONS entry records it
description: PRD 7.4 step 1 includes 'The pool is on the ticker's allowlist', and failing step 1 makes the leg REFUSED_TICKER with its USDG sent to spend. SPEC 9 step 5.1 says the same. _guard returns REFUSED_TICKER only when the allowlist is empty. A pool off a non-empty allowlist reverts PoolNotAllowed (line 387) for split and for settle. The behavior is safer, since a public caller can't push equity into spend by passing a bad pool. But it contradicts the PRD and SPEC, and the only place it's recorded is a code comment. The build contract says a PRD conflict is reported, not chosen.
scenario: The keeper passes a pool that the timelock removed after the keeper cached the list. The PRD expects a REFUSED_TICKER receipt with the equity in spend. The code reverts and writes no receipt. test_fork_poolNotAllowed_reverts encodes the deviation as the acceptance behavior.
impact: Spec drift. The keeper, verifier and claim ledger built from SPEC 9 will expect a REFUSED_TICKER receipt that never comes. Reviewers will flag the PRD mismatch.
fix: Keep the revert but add a DECISIONS entry (or ask the owner, since the PRD wins), and update SPEC 9 step 5.1 and SPEC 10 so step 1 reads: ticker inactive, no feed or empty allowlist gives REFUSED_TICKER, and a trigger pool off a non-empty allowlist reverts PoolNotAllowed.

title: An empty pool allowlist on an active ticker turns every split and every bucket into spend
description: When poolsOf(tickerId) is empty, _guard returns REFUSE_TICKER even though the ticker is still active. Split sends each new equity part to spend. Settle, which the keeper or anyone after the grace can call, sends whole buckets to spend as REFUSED_TICKER. TokenSource.setPool(id, pool, false) can empty the list (TokenSource.sol 276-290). Swapping in a new pool takes two separate 48-hour operations. If the removal runs first, there's a window where queued equity across all accounts can be pushed to spend by anyone. D-009 Q24 and PRD 9 tie that outcome to removing the ticker, not to rotating pools.
scenario: The timelock executes setPool(SPY, oldPool, false) before setPool(SPY, newPool, true). During that gap, keeper splits for SPY rules write REFUSED_TICKER, and a public caller settles every SPY bucket past its grace into spend.
impact: A routine admin operation in the wrong order changes owners' allocation outcomes. No funds move out of the account, but the equity share for affected payments is lost to spend for good.
fix: Treat an empty allowlist on an active ticker as a QUEUE reason, or revert NoPool, and keep REFUSED_TICKER for removal and missing feeds. Or make TokenSource refuse a removal that would leave an active ticker with no pools. At minimum, document add-before-remove in the timelock runbook and the proposal script.

title: The caller-chosen quote makes the owner's slippageBps decorative for keeper and public triggers
description: minOut is built from job.quote, which the trigger caller supplies. Any non-zero quote is accepted, so a quote of 1 gives a minOut close to zero. After the grace, a public caller can wrap split in a contract that pushes the allowlisted pool up to just under premiumCapBps above the feed, calls split, and sells back in the same transaction. The default keeper EOA could do the same, through EIP-7702 or by sending transactions in order on the FCFS sequencer. D-009 Q21 accepts that the premium cap is the real bound, but the rule still exposes slippageBps as if it protected the owner.
scenario: Rule premiumCapBps 500, the pool trades 0.2 percent below the feed. An attacker extracts about 5.2 percent of each equity part, minus pool fees, on every public-triggered buy.
impact: Loss per buy is capped at the owner's chosen premium cap. It's within spec, but the UI and rule suggest slippageBps also bounds it.
fix: For KEEPER and PUBLIC triggers, floor minOut at the feed-implied amount: amountIn * 10^(18+8-6) / answer * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000, so slippageBps bounds the fill against the feed. Otherwise drop slippageBps from the rule for non-owner triggers and say so in the copy.

title: Code inside the account batch can forge PremiumAboveCap and make split write a fake PREMIUM queue receipt
description: _buy catches any revert from executeBuy that is 36 bytes long and starts with the PremiumAboveCap selector, then treats it as the module's own premium check and copies the encoded int256 into receipt.premiumBps. executeFromExecutor (SleeveBuy.sol line 68) bubbles raw revert data from everything that runs inside the batch: the account implementation, a Kernel executor hook the owner set on Sleeve's executor config (preCheck/postCheck run inside executeFromExecutor), the USDG facets, the stock token's beacon implementation, the router and the pool. Any of them can revert with PremiumAboveCap(x) for any x.
scenario: Owner installs Sleeve with an executor hook whose postCheck reverts PremiumAboveCap(-4242). Or the account is a custom ERC-7579 implementation, or a stock token implementation is upgraded to do it. The keeper's split catches the revert, queues the equity with reason PREMIUM, and writes a QUEUED receipt with premiumBps = -4242, a value the module never measured. test/audit/reentrancy_DustAndForgedRevert.t.sol test_forgedPremiumAboveCapIsCaughtAsPremiumQueue shows the forged receipt being written.
impact: The receipt log, which is the product's trust surface, can carry premium numbers and PREMIUM reasons the guard never produced, and the verifier can't tell them apart from real ones. It also turns any revert inside the batch into a soft queue where the spec says the whole call should revert (D-009 Q12). Only the owner (against their own account) or the issuer can trigger it, so there is no third-party fund loss.
fix: In SleeveBuy._swap, wrap executeFromExecutor in try/catch. If the inner revert data starts with the PremiumAboveCap selector, re-revert with a different error (for example BatchReverted(bytes)). Otherwise bubble it unchanged, so the router's minimum-out error still surfaces. Then the only PremiumAboveCap that can leave executeBuy is the one SleeveBuy.execute raises itself at line 53.

title: USDG pause or freeze reverts split and settle wholesale instead of queueing or refusing with a named reason
description: The guard checks only the stock token side: the registry's isBlocked on the account and pool, token.paused() and oraclePaused() (PriceGuard.checkToken, lines 192-197). It never reads USDG's paused() or isFrozen() for the account, SwapRouter02 or the pool. USDG.approve checks msg.sender and the spender, and transferFrom checks from, to and msg.sender, all under whenNotPaused. So a USDG pause, or a freeze on the account, the router or a pool, makes the executeFromExecutor batch revert with ContractPaused or AddressFrozen. _buy rethrows that error, the whole split reverts, and not even the spend share is booked or a receipt written. This contrasts with the stock token pause, which queues with PAUSED, and with build-contract rule 3, which calls for named custom errors.
scenario: Paxos freezes SwapRouter02 in USDG, or pauses USDG for a day. Every keeper and public split where the guard would buy reverts AddressFrozen or ContractPaused with no receipt. Keepers retry in a loop, and settle reverts the same way. A frozen pool only blocks triggers that pick it, but a frozen router blocks every buy.
impact: Liveness and observability only. Funds stay in the account and the issuer freeze is a disclosed risk (PRD 9), but the receipt log is silent through the event and the failure isn't named.
fix: In the guard, read usdg.paused() and usdg.isFrozen(x) for the account, router and pool. Queue with PAUSED when USDG is paused or the router or pool is frozen, refuse or revert with a named error when the account is frozen, and treat a failed probe as not frozen. At minimum, catch the batch revert in _buy and rethrow it wrapped in a named error such as BuyReverted(bytes).

title: Dust transfers plus observe() can push the public-trigger fallback back forever
description: _requireSplitGrace needs unsorted <= observedUnsorted, and observe() restarts the clock whenever unsorted grows (line 73). So any transfer of 1 base unit before the grace ends makes the public split revert, and the next observe starts a fresh 3,600-second grace. settle's ready time also takes max(since, observedAt), so the same trick delays a public settle.
scenario: The keeper is down and a 500 USDG payment waits. A griefer sends 1 base unit every 59 minutes and calls observe. The public split never becomes callable. Verified by contracts/test/audit/funds_Liveness.t.sol::test_dustGriefsPublicSplit.
impact: The liveness fallback for a dead keeper can be held off indefinitely for gas plus dust. Funds wait as USDG under the owner's control.
fix: Keep the observation's start time and let a public split sort at most observedUnsorted, leaving the newer excess for the next observation, rather than reverting when unsorted has grown. Apply the same idea to settle, so observedAt only moves forward when the bucket itself changed.

title: The module-wide transient reentrancy lock lets any self-installed contract make other accounts' Sleeve calls fail while it holds control
description: ReentrancyGuardTransient uses one lock slot for the whole module, not one per account. split and settle hold that lock while SleeveBuy calls account.executeFromExecutor (SleeveBuy.sol 68), which hands control to the account. Any contract can install the module on itself (D-015). As OWNER it can call split on its own ledger and get control inside executeFromExecutor with the lock held. Every Sleeve entry point reached from there reverts ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall for every account, including beginOwnerOp, which the app puts first in every owner UserOp (I14). The attacker can then run the module's own batch to pass the buy postconditions, so the outer split succeeds and nothing it did is rolled back.
scenario: A malicious bundler wraps EntryPoint.handleOps (v0.7 has no EOA-only caller check, unlike v0.8) inside its fake account's executeFromExecutor during its own split, which needs at least a 1 USDG clip and an open market. Each honest owner UserOp in that bundle passes validation and then reverts at beginOwnerOp in execution. handleOps does not revert, so the victims pay actualGasCost to the bundler. PoC: test/audit/transient_Audit.t.sol::test_globalLockFailsOtherAccountsOwnerOpNestedInAnotherBuy. A victim owner op nested inside another account's split fails with ReentrancyGuardReentrantCall and its transfer does not happen.
impact: A bundler gets a cheap way to force execution-phase failures on any Sleeve owner's bracketed UserOp and still collect gas. Owners pay for failed ops and their actions are delayed. No ledger corruption.
fix: Key the lock per account. owner entry points (onInstall, onUninstall, setRule, pause, resume, setKeeper, begin, end, release) would lock on msg.sender, and split, settle and observe on the target account, with a transient slot derived like SleeveState.beginSlot. That keeps same-account reentrancy blocked without one account's buy blocking every other account. If the global lock stays, document the bundler griefing vector in DECISIONS and SECURITY.

title: defaultKeeper is immutable and shared by every account, so a leaked KEEPER key cannot be rotated centrally
description: An install without a keeper writes the immutable defaultKeeper into acct.keeper. KEEPER is one EOA (D-004) and becomes the keeper of every account the app installs. The PRD threat table says 'Trigger timed for the worst price inside the cap' is handled because the keeper or the owner triggers first and the public waits out the grace. A stolen keeper key keeps the no-grace trigger, with a caller-chosen quote (minOut near zero, Q21) and pool, on every account. The only fix is for each owner to sign setKeeper. New installs keep getting the leaked default for the life of the module.
scenario: KEEPER leaks. The attacker pushes an allowlisted pool up to just under each account's premium cap against the feed, calls split or settle as KEEPER for every account with unsorted or pending USDG, then sells back. Without the key, a public caller can only do this after the grace, by which time the honest keeper has already sorted.
impact: The attacker can take up to premiumCapBps (up to 500 bps) of every equity buy across all default-keeper accounts until each owner rotates. The power is the same as a public caller's after the grace, so this is within the PRD's wording, but there is no central way to revoke it.
fix: Treat acct.keeper == address(0) as 'use the module's current default', read from a pointer that SleeveTimelock can rotate or that the deployer can only clear, and use a separate sentinel such as address(1) for 'no keeper'. Otherwise, document a forced setKeeper migration in the app and keeper runbook and make the app pass an explicit keeper at install.

title: Any contract can self-register, get the default keeper, and write authentic-looking FILLED receipts and lots with fabricated fills into the global log
description: onInstall accepts any msg.sender, and a zero keeper in the data assigns defaultKeeper. SleeveTrade._enter (SleeveTrade.sol:479-496) only checks that the caller-chosen account answers isModuleInstalled(2, module) == 1 (_listsModule, line 500), which any contract can do. SleeveBuy then calls account.executeFromExecutor (SleeveBuy.sol:68) and trusts the account's balance deltas. A fake account can spend exactly amountIn USDG to any address and mint or pull stock tokens from elsewhere, with no swap at all. The module then writes a FILLED receipt with venue Uniswap v3, an allowlisted pool, the real feed round, a premium the account chose, a stored hash that recomputes cleanly, and a lot. PoC test/audit/aa_FakeAccountReceipts.t.sol passes: FILLED, tokensOut 1e30, premiumBps below -9,000, and the router never received USDG. The same registration also gives every fake account Sleeve's default keeper, so a keeper that triggers every Installed account with keeper == defaultKeeper sends real transactions into attacker code. That code can burn the gas limit on purpose, or succeed while using a lot of gas.
scenario: An attacker deploys FakeFillAccount, calls onInstall with keeper 0 and the default rule, sends itself 500 USDG, then calls split(self, allowlistedPool, quote) as OWNER. Its executeFromExecutor sends 50 USDG to a sink and mints tokens. Receipt N is FILLED at roughly -10,000 bps premium, Lot N exists, and receiptHash(N) matches the event. The attacker repeats this to fill the public receipt log, or registers many accounts so the keeper keeps paying gas on them.
impact: No user funds are at risk. The receipt log is Sleeve's trust surface, and any README, HP1 or verifier number that aggregates receipts module-wide can be skewed with fabricated fills that pass hash recomputation. The default keeper can be griefed for ETH. The isolation claim from g6 notes (state keyed by msg.sender) holds for ledgers but not for the shared receipt log or the shared keeper.
fix: Contract side: do not give self-registered callers the default keeper by default. Require an explicit keeper in install data, or let the keeper opt in through an off-chain allowlist. Verifier, keeper and metrics side, documented as a requirement in SPEC: count a receipt only when the account's code is the Kernel v3.1 ERC-1967 proxy (61-byte runtime with implementation slot 0xBAC8...4b4D) and the FILLED or SETTLED receipt's tx has a matching pool Swap event with recipient == account and the same amounts. The keeper should apply the same codehash filter and a hard gas cap before it triggers any account.

title: onUninstall wipes the module's state even when Kernel still lists the executor (uninstallModule with type 4/5/6, or a direct call)
description: Kernel v3.1 uninstallModule for types 4, 5 and 6 force-calls module.onUninstall through ModuleLib without checking that the module is installed as that type (lib/kernel/src/Kernel.sol:457-482). The account can also call onUninstall directly from a batch. SleeveModule.onUninstall releases the buckets and deletes the account's state without checking that the account has actually stopped listing it as an executor. The result is the reverse of the drift D-019 handles: Kernel lists the executor, but isInitialized is false. From then on every split and settle reverts NotInstalled, and USDG that arrives is never sorted until a reinstall puts it all into spend through the snapshot.
scenario: The owner's client, an SDK helper or a dapp-built batch signed by the owner sends uninstallModule(4, sleeveModule, "") by mistake, for example while removing an executor hook. Kernel calls Sleeve.onUninstall, which releases the buckets and deletes the ledgers while executorConfig(sleeve).hook stays address(1). Paychecks then sit unsorted. When the app reinstalls, the snapshot moves them all to spend, so the equity share of that income is never invested.
impact: Only a signed owner action can trigger this, so no third party can exploit it. It silently stops the product for that account and causes a spec deviation: income during the gap goes to spend instead of being split.
fix: In onUninstall, check _listsModule(msg.sender) first and revert if the account still lists the module. Kernel's executor path clears executorConfig before it calls onUninstall, so a real uninstall passes the check, and Kernel swallows the revert on the wrong-type paths, so state is kept. Optionally, onInstall can also require _listsModule(msg.sender), because Kernel writes executorConfig before onInstall. That rejects installs as a fallback or hook type.

title: Observation clock survives an owner outflow, so a later payment is publicly splittable with no grace
description: observedAt and observedUnsorted are a cached snapshot of unsorted. They are only cleared by a split or settle that writes a receipt (SleeveTrade._clearObservation, lines 105 and 296). _bookOwnerOutflow (SleeveModule.sol 428-446), which can drain unsorted at endOwnerOp, never clears or clamps them. Neither does the reconcile branch of split (SleeveTrade.sol 97-100, which returns before _clearObservation) or release. After the owner spends the observed income, the stale observedUnsorted still 'covers' any later income up to that size, and observedAt is already more than an hour old.
scenario: Payment of 500 USDG lands and a stranger calls observe (T0, 500). Before any split, the owner withdraws 600 USDG in a bracketed batch: spend 100 then unsorted 500, so unsorted is 0 and the observation is still (T0, 500). Five hours later a new 400 USDG payment arrives, and a stranger calls split in the same block. _requireSplitGrace sees covered (400 <= 500) and readyAt = T0 + 3600 in the past, so the PUBLIC split succeeds immediately. PoC: test/audit/transient_Audit.t.sol::test_staleObservationAfterOwnerOutflowSkipsGrace passes.
impact: This breaks D-009 Q15 ('a payment cannot be pre-aged') and takes away the keeper's one-hour priority window for the new payment. The public caller picks the pool and the quote, so only the premium cap bounds the fill (Q21). No funds move outside the rule, but the public trigger runs on terms the owner's keeper never saw.
fix: After an owner outflow in _bookOwnerOutflow, clear the observation or clamp observedUnsorted to the new unsorted. Do the same in the split reconcile branch and in release/_releaseBuckets when unsorted and buckets are empty. Add a unit test: observe, bracketed withdraw, new payment, public split reverts GracePeriodActive.

title: The 48-hour admin delay is never bound on chain: TokenSource, the calendar and the module accept any contract as timelock
description: TokenSource (line 168) and SessionCalendarExtension (line 131) check only timelock_.code.length != 0. The SleeveModule constructor (lines 94-115) checks USDG, factory and decimals, but never that tokenSource.timelock() == calendar.timelock() or that this timelock enforces MIN_DELAY_FLOOR. ArbOS 61 on chain 4663 supports EIP-7702, so a delegated EOA has code and passes the check. SleeveTimelock's constructor also accepts address(0) among executors, which its own NatSpec warns about.
scenario: The deploy script passes DEPLOYER (7702-delegated), a plain TimelockController with a 0 delay, or two different timelocks. Every check passes. removeTicker, setPool, appendYear and replaceFutureSwitch then run with no 48-hour public window, and the module, which is immutable, is bound to them for good.
impact: The documented admin bound (D-004, D-018: 'behind a 48-hour timelock with a public event') rests on deploy-script discipline and nothing on chain enforces it. If it is wrong, the admin can open a closed calendar instant or swap pools at once.
fix: In the SleeveModule constructor, require tokenSource.timelock() == calendar.timelock(), that SleeveTimelock(t).MIN_DELAY_FLOOR() == 172_800 and t.getMinDelay() >= that floor, and optionally pin extcodehash. In the SleeveTimelock constructor, revert when an executor or proposer is address(0) or when either list is empty.

title: Session type is fixed at construction, so a ticker that loses overnight trading cannot be moved to REGULAR
description: A ticker's sessionType is written once, in _list, from the TokenSource constructor. TokenSource exposes only removeTicker and setPool, and nothing lists a ticker again (I10). The REGULAR branch in SessionCalendar.decide and _openedAt, which is the safe mapping the research names (session-calendar.md Q2) for a ticker that loses overnight tradability, therefore can't be reached in production. PRD 7.4 takes the per-ticker session type from the issuer's tradability field, which can change. The calendar's in-range writes (addClosure, addEarlyClose) only act on whole days or the 13:00/17:00 early close, so they can't express 'closed 20:00 to 09:30'.
scenario: The overnight venue stops for weeks, as Blue Ocean ATS did after 5 Aug 2024, or the issuer flips tradingCapabilities.overnight for NVDA. The Chainlink 24/5 feed then holds the 20:00 round overnight. SleeveTrade._guard (line 377) still gets open=true, openedAt is the Sunday 20:00 reopen, and the held round passes both the 25-hour age check and updatedAt >= openedAt. Suppose after-hours news drops the real price 8 percent. An attacker holding tokens lifts the thin overnight pool to just under the held answer times (1 + premiumCap) and fires a public settle on a queued bucket once its grace has run. The module buys about 8 percent plus the cap above the real market, every night until the timelock acts. The only lever is removeTicker, after 48 hours, and it's permanent: the ticker can never be listed again, and every later equity share goes to spend.
impact: Conditional overpayment against a held reference during an overnight outage, bounded by how far the real market moved plus the premium cap. The only remedy permanently delists the ticker.
fix: Add a timelocked TokenSource.tightenSessionType(id, newType) that allows only ALL_DAY to REGULAR or anything to NONE, emits an event and bumps a version the receipts record. Like addClosure, refuse it once it would change an answer for an instant already past. As an alternative, give SessionCalendarExtension a per-type overnight-closure range. Record the decision in DECISIONS.md either way.

title: Premium cap treats USDG as exactly 1 USD, so the USD premium can pass the cap by up to the depeg tolerance
description: exceedsPremium (and premiumBps, used for the receipt) compares USDG spent, in USDG, with tokensOut * answer, where answer is the Chainlink stock price in USD. The USDG/USD answer that checkUsdg reads in the same guard pass is only used as a pass or fail band (plus or minus 50 bps). It is never used to turn the USD reference into USDG. Any USDG/USD value inside the band therefore adds straight onto the owner's cap when measured against the USD reference that PRD 7.4 item 8 and claim C2 describe.
scenario: USDG/USD reads 1.005e8, which passes DEPEG at 50 bps. The rule cap is 100 bps and the SPY feed reads 100 USD. A fill of 101 USDG for 1e18 token units passes exceedsPremium, and the receipt shows premiumBps = 100. In USD the owner paid 101.505 USD for a 100 USD reference, a 150.5 bps premium. PoC: test/audit/arithmetic_Premium.t.sol::ArithmeticPremiumParTest.test_usdgPremiumAddsToCapInUsdTerms (passes).
impact: A buy can pay up to about cap + 50 bps over the USD market reference (150.5 bps at the 100 bps default, about 552 bps at the 500 bps maximum) while the receipt and the verifier report it as within the cap. The C2 metric, which is premium over the market reference, is understated by the same amount. The loss is bounded by the depeg tolerance, so this is LOW.
fix: Convert the reference into USDG before comparing. Pass usdgAnswer into exceedsPremium/premiumBps (and exceedsDiscount/discountBps for sells) and compare usdgSpent * usdgAnswer * 10^scale * 10,000 against tokensOut * answer * 10^feedDecimals * (10,000 + cap), using the same 512-bit products. If par is a deliberate choice, add a DECISIONS.md entry and state on receipts that the premium is in USDG at par.

title: A contract posing as an account can write genuine module receipts that record fills at any price
description: Any contract can call onInstall on itself (D-015), answer isModuleInstalled with true, and run executeFromExecutor however it likes. SleeveBuy._swap measures only the account's own balance deltas, so tokens the fake account pulls from its own stash count as tokensOut. The module then writes a FILLED receipt with the real module address, a global id, a stored hash, the allowlisted pool and a premium far below the feed. D-015 says a fake account reaches only its own state, but the receipt log and lot ids are shared and the receipt is the trust surface.
scenario: An attacker deploys a TamperingAccount, installs the module, gets paid 500 USDG and runs split as OWNER. During the batch it also moves 1,000,000 tokens into itself from a helper. The module emits a FILLED receipt with premiumBps below -9,000 and pool set to the SPY allowlisted pool. PoC test/audit/access_Observe.t.sol::test_access_fakeAccountMintsAFilledReceiptAtAnyPrice passes.
impact: Receipts and aggregates built from ReceiptWritten (HP1 campaign numbers, README stats, a 'best fill' shown in the app or verify page) can be filled with fabricated fills that carry the module's authority. No user funds are at risk.
fix: Tie the fill to the pool in SleeveBuy: read the pool's USDG and token balances before and after, and require that the pool received exactly amountIn USDG and released exactly tokensOut tokens. In the verifier and every aggregate script, also accept a receipt only when the account's code is a Kernel v3.1 proxy with the expected implementation and the fill transaction's Transfer logs run between the pool and the account.

title: The trigger's quote makes the owner's slippage cap void for keeper and public triggers. An atomic sandwich fills at the premium cap every time
description: minOut = amount * quote / 1e6 * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000, and quote comes from the caller. _enter checks only quote != 0. A public caller after the grace, or the keeper with no grace, can pass quote = 1, which gives minOut of a few base units of an 18-decimal token. The only remaining bound is the premium cap against the Chainlink answer. FCFS ordering doesn't help, because the public caller can push the pool, trigger split or settle, and unwind inside one transaction. D-009 Q21 and PRD line 429 accept the premium cap as the bound, but the PRD (line 181) still describes a working 50 bps slippage cap. In practice the extraction is deterministic and repeatable, not just residual manipulation. Two things widen it past the nominal cap. The premium is measured against a USD feed with USDG treated as exactly 1 (up to the 50 bps depeg tolerance). And intra-session the stock feed can lag the market by up to its 0.5 percent deviation trigger.
scenario: Rule: 100 bps cap, 50 bps slippage. The keeper is down for an hour, so the public grace elapses. An attacker contract buys SPY in the allowlisted pool to about 99 bps above the feed, calls split(account, pool, 1), then sells back. PoC test/audit/modern_PublicQuote.t.sol passes: status FILLED, minOut 49 base units, premiumBps between 51 and 100. A compromised default keeper (a single EOA, D-004) can do this to every account without waiting out the grace, by sequencing its own transactions or by delegating with EIP-7702.
impact: Each equity buy reached by a non-owner trigger can be made to pay close to the full premium cap, default 1 percent and up to 5 percent, plus feed lag and USDG/USD drift. The attacker keeps the overpayment. It also biases claim C2 (price discipline), because premiums cluster at the cap.
fix: For non-owner triggers, don't trust the caller's quote. Floor minOut on chain at the feed-implied output: feedOut = amount * 10^(tokenDec + feedDec - usdgDec) / answer, and minOut = max(callerMinOut, feedOut * (10,000 - slippageBps) / 10,000). This makes slippage a bound relative to the feed and closes the atomic sandwich beyond that bound. If the cap must stay the bound, fix the PRD and app copy that describe a slippage cap against the trigger's quote, and record the residual in the claim ledger.

title: Lots for component 6 are keyed to this module instance and never follow tokens that leave outside Sleeve
description: Lots live in this module's storage, and Q30 makes tokens outside lots unsellable through Sleeve. PRD 10 requires a new module version whenever the issuer disclosure changes, and PRD 13 says a new version is a new install. Every lot bought under the old version then becomes unsellable through sell-back, which is the M0 cash path. tokensRemaining also never drops when the owner moves tokens out under I11, so a sell by amount can attribute proceeds to lots whose tokens are gone.
scenario: The issuer edits its disclosure text, and Sleeve ships v2 with the new hash. The owner installs v2. All existing SPY holdings have no v2 lots and can't be sold through Sleeve.
impact: A spec conflict for component 6. A routine disclosure update breaks the sell-back promise in PRD 7.5.
fix: Before writing component 6, decide on lot migration: a v2 import of v1 lots verified against v1 receipt hashes, or a sell path for unlotted balances under the same guard. Cap any sell at min(lot remaining, the account's token balance).

title: Income arriving before an outside pull is reconciled is netted against the shortfall and isn't split in full
description: split reconciles only when unsorted is 0. If USDG leaves through an old approval (a shortfall) and a payment lands before any split reconciles, unsorted = balance - spend - pending already absorbs the shortfall. Part of the payment silently refills the spend ledger instead of being split.
scenario: spend 100, an outside pull of 100, then a 1,000 USDG payment before the keeper runs. The split sorts 900 and invests 10 percent of 900, not 1,000.
impact: Some of the payment that should have been invested goes to spend instead. It's inherent to balance-based accounting and matches the PRD formula.
fix: Have the keeper call split as soon as previewSplit shows a shortfall above zero (it reconciles), and document the netting in DECISIONS.md and the receipt explainer.

title: Any unsorted amount, down to 1 base unit, makes the keeper pay for a full split and receipt
description: split proceeds for any unsorted > 0. At default rules, a 1-wei payment gives equityPart 0, which still writes a QUEUED CLIP receipt, and a sub-clip equity part runs the whole guard (about 304k gas measured for QUEUED CLIP). An attacker spending about 50k gas per dust transfer across many installed accounts makes a keeper that splits everything spend several times as much gas.
scenario: An attacker sends 1 base unit of USDG to 1,000 installed accounts. A keeper that splits any unsorted balance writes 1,000 receipts.
impact: Drains the keeper's gas funding and adds noise to the receipt log. Public triggers pay their own gas, so only the keeper is exposed.
fix: Keeper policy: skip a split while unsorted is below a threshold (for example rule.minClip * 10,000 / equityBps), unless the oldest unsorted inflow is older than a set age. Optionally the contract could refuse a non-owner split below a floor, but the off-chain threshold is enough.

title: A removed ticker's bucket below the current clip can't be refused to spend by settle
description: _settle checks BelowClip before the guard, so the D-009 Q24 path (a removed ticker sends its bucket to spend as REFUSED_TICKER) applies only to buckets at or above the current rule's minClip. Smaller buckets wait until the owner calls release.
scenario: An AAPL bucket of 10 USDG under a 25 USDG clip. The timelock removes AAPL. Keeper settle reverts BelowClip, and the bucket stays pending until the owner releases it.
impact: Small deviation from Q24. Funds stay safe and the owner can release them.
fix: Run the step 1 and step 2 refusal checks before BelowClip in _settle, or note the exception in Q24.

title: bucket.reason is the latest queue reason and settle never updates it, so the five-day same-reason prompt can't be driven from chain state
description: _queue overwrites bucket.reason with each new part's reason, while since stays at the first queue time. Settle reverts GuardNotClear with no state change (line 281), so the reason a bucket is actually waiting on, such as PREMIUM after a weekend SESSION queue, is never recorded. PRD 7.4 asks the app to prompt 'after five days queued for the same reason'.
scenario: A bucket is queued SESSION on Saturday. From Monday every settle simulation fails PREMIUM. bucketOf still shows SESSION with since on Saturday.
impact: The app or keeper has to rebuild the reason history from receipts and simulations. Bucket state alone gives a wrong prompt.
fix: Spell out in SPEC that the prompt comes from keeper simulations and receipts, or store a per-reason since that settle can refresh.

title: The commit snapshot has no stateful invariant suite for I1, I4 and I8
description: SPEC 17 maps I1, I4, I6 and I8 to an invariant suite, and PRD C3 says 'tested by invariant fuzzing'. At e16bb96 those invariants are covered by stateless fuzz tests (1,000 to 2,000 runs) and fork tests. No invariant_ functions exist for the module. The handler-based suite in contracts/test/invariant/ is untracked and not part of the audited commit. Otherwise, component 5 acceptance is met on the fork with real role holders: fills on all five D-010 pools by keeper, owner (handleOps) and public; every QUEUED reason (SESSION and STALE at the real weekend and reopen blocks, with vm.mockCall only for post-reopen rounds); REFUSED_TICKER through a real timelocked removal; REFUSED_ACCOUNT through the real registry blocker; and the minimum-out revert from the real SwapRouter02. Partial fill uses a wrapper router, and DEPEG is covered by age only on the fork (the price band is unit-only). REFUSED_TICKER for an empty allowlist is unit-only.
scenario: A reviewer checks C3 and SPEC 17 against the commit and finds no stateful suite.
impact: Claims 1.9 and 3.7 stay PENDING until the suite is committed.
fix: Commit the stateful suite before component 5 is accepted, and list in PROGRESS which fork tests use mocks: Weekend latestRoundData, PartialFillRouter and the ArbSys etch.

title: Measured silent-skip window for the uninstall release: callGasLimit from about 120k to about 320k removes the module and skips onUninstall
description: This is a known Kernel behavior (D-019, g6 section 7), quantified here with all four buckets full on the fork at block 78,312,136 under --isolate (test/audit/aa_UninstallGas.t.sol). At callGasLimit 250k and 300k the UserOp succeeds, Kernel no longer lists the module, ModuleUninstallResult is false and isInitialized stays true, so no RELEASED receipts are written. At 330k and above, the release completes. Without --isolate, 120k to 300k fails silently and 150k reverts the whole op. The app floor of 400k leaves about 70k of headroom on forge's EVM, which is not ArbOS, so ArbSys and L1 pricing are not modeled. A bundler's eth_estimateUserOperationGas, which binary-searches for the lowest callGasLimit that does not revert, will land inside the silent window, because the outer call succeeds whether or not onUninstall does.
scenario: The app, or any other ERC-4337 client the owner uses, lets the bundler estimate callGasLimit for uninstallModule(2, sleeve). The estimate comes back near 200k. The op succeeds, buckets stay pending in module state, and no Uninstalled or RELEASED event is emitted.
impact: No funds move, because the module holds none. The ledger and receipts stay stale until a second uninstall or a reinstall, so the verifier and app show pending buckets for an account that no longer has the module.
fix: Keep the app-side 400k floor, and never accept an estimate. Assert ModuleUninstallResult(module, true). As defense in depth, add a permissionless prune(account) that runs only when _listsModule(account) is false and acct.installed is true. It releases the buckets with RELEASED receipts and deletes state, so anyone, including the keeper, can close out a skipped release without the owner.

title: Sell-back must feed the bracket's module delta or sale proceeds are booked to spend twice
description: Component 6 is not written yet. The bracket math in endOwnerOp is ownerDelta = balanceNow - balanceAtBegin - moduleDelta, and today only _recordFill (SleeveTrade.sol 461) calls recordModuleDelta. A sell-back run by the owner inside its bracket (SPEC: 'normally inside an owner bracket') that credits proceeds to spend directly, without recordModuleDelta(+usdgOut), would have endOwnerOp book the same proceeds again as an owner inflow.
scenario: The owner sells a lot for 100 USDG inside [beginOwnerOp, sell, endOwnerOp]. The sell credits spend +100, endOwnerOp sees ownerDelta = +100, and spend is credited +100 again, so spend is above the real balance. The next split reconciles, but in the meantime the ledger says 100 USDG of spend that does not exist, and that can be pulled from buckets on the next owner outflow.
impact: An accounting error in the module about to be written. This is guidance for component 6, not a bug in the snapshot.
fix: In the sell path, call SleeveState.recordModuleDelta(account, int256(usdgOut)) after measuring proceeds by balance delta, mirroring _recordFill. Add a fork test with a bracketed sell that checks spend equals balance minus pending after endOwnerOp.

title: Lot plumbing has no ownership check: component 6 must enforce lot.account and the ticker
description: transitionLot checks only that the lot exists and that the status transition is allowed. It does not check the caller, the account, the ticker or tokensRemaining. Lot ids are global (they are receipt ids), and lots and lotQueues outlive uninstall. Fake accounts (see the receipt finding) also create lots in the same id space.
scenario: If component 6 adds a sell-by-lot entry point that takes a lotId and trusts it, one account could transition, and corrupt the attribution of, another account's lot. A lot could also be sold under the wrong ticker's pool and guard.
impact: Nothing today. It is a precondition for component 6 to be correct.
fix: In component 6, require lot.account == the account being sold for (and msg.sender == account for owner-only sells and the off-hours override) and lot.tickerId == tickerId. Decrement tokensRemaining and measure tokens leaving by balance delta, because the owner can move tokens out of the account outside Sleeve (I11).

title: A split whose equity part rounds to zero writes QUEUED/CLIP although nothing is queued
description: When floor(unsorted * equityBps / 10,000) == 0, which covers every split under a 0-bps equity rule and dust payments under small shares, _sort writes status QUEUED with reason CLIP, usdgQueued 0 and no bucket change, and the whole amount goes to spend. I2 holds. The status still says money is waiting when it is not.
scenario: The rule is spendBps 10,000 and equityBps 0, and a 500 USDG payment arrives. The keeper's split writes a QUEUED/CLIP receipt with usdgToSpend 500e6 and usdgQueued 0. The inbox would show a queued item that no settle can ever clear.
impact: Misleading receipts and app state only. No funds are affected.
fix: Record this case with a status that means the whole amount went to spend, or keep QUEUED/CLIP but have the app and verifier key on usdgQueued == 0 and document it in SPEC section 13.

title: Expired calendar coverage reads as an ordinary SESSION queue: the OUT_OF_RANGE reason is dropped and nothing warns before the 2028 cliff
description: _guard reads calendar.sessionState and throws away the calendar's Reason. An expired calendar (OUT_OF_RANGE) and a normal weekend therefore produce the same QUEUED/SESSION receipt, the same preview and the same GuardNotClear(SESSION). SPEC section 9 step 4 merges them on purpose, but the build contract's 'no silent fallback' rule and research Q8 expected coverage expiry to be visible. The extension starts with endDay = 1 Jan 2028. Dec 31 2027 is a Friday and Jan 1 2028 a Saturday, so the first instant that changes is Sun 2 Jan 2028 20:00 EST (1830474000), the open for Mon 3 Jan. appendYear(2028) has to be scheduled on the 48-hour timelock before about 31 Dec 2027 20:00 EST.
scenario: No one schedules appendYear(2028) in time. From 1830474000 every split queues and every settle reverts GuardNotClear(SESSION) on a normal Monday. The receipts look the same as a weekend's, so the keeper and verifier can't tell an expired calendar from a closed market unless they also call coverageEnd().
impact: Liveness only, with funds waiting in buckets until the year is appended. The risk is operational: the failure is silent.
fix: Carry the calendar Reason into Guard and either add a COVERAGE reason (types say the numbering never changes, so append it) or put the calendar reason in previews. Have the keeper alert when coverageEnd() - now < 30 days, and add a deploy-checklist item to schedule appendYear(2028) by early December 2027.

title: A trigger-supplied quote can make the minOut mulDiv panic instead of reverting with a named error
description: minOut = Math.mulDiv(Math.mulDiv(amount, quote, 1e6), 10,000 - slippageBps, 10,000). quote is an unbounded uint256 from the keeper or a public caller, and the only check is that it is non-zero. When amount * quote / 1e6 does not fit in a uint256, OpenZeppelin's mulDiv calls Panic(0x11). The build contract says every failed check reverts with a named custom error, and LedgerMath states that no input makes a function panic.
scenario: The keeper calls split(account, pool, type(uint256).max) on a 500 USDG payment. The call reverts with Panic(0x11) from the minOut computation. PoC: test/audit/arithmetic_Premium.t.sol::ArithmeticQuotePanicTest.test_hugeQuotePanics (passes).
impact: Only the caller's own transaction fails and no state changes. The keeper and verifier get an unlabeled panic in place of a decodable error.
fix: Bound the quote up front, for example revert QuoteTooLarge(quote) when quote > type(uint256).max / amount * 1e6, or compute the product with Math.mul512 and revert with a named error when the high word is at least 1e6.
